title: Color spaces, gamma and image math
hook: Half black and half white is not 0.5 in light: what blending and shrinking do to sRGB codes, and why SaveImage truncates.

verified.claim: sRGB curves in the lab match the formulas in the CSS Color 4 sample code and in srgb_to_linear.
The real ImageBlend and ImageColorSpace give 0.5 and 0.73536 on black and white.
verified.ref: the graph b_blend_light, and the nodes in a Python session

verified.claim: LoadImage goes first through VideoFromFile, which for 8-bit formats divides by 255 in float32. PNG and JPEG files came back with EXIF orientation applied, all 256 codes unchanged after SaveImage's cast, and the same numbers with a color profile embedded. SaveImage clips and casts to uint8.
verified.ref: comfy_api.input_impl.VideoFromFile in a Python session, and nodes.py

verified.claim: ImageBlend does a lerp and clamps.

unchecked: We assume the stored codes are sRGB, which is the usual case. Our profile test used one synthetic profile on PNG and JPEG. We did not test a real wide-gamut file, or files above 8 bits.
We did not measure the latent space of any model, so the lesson says nothing about what a VAE does to colour.
The truncation figures are for uniformly random values, and real images are not uniform.
